Hi Mario,

Thanks for writing, and for the thinking you have put into this. Let me take the two parts separately.

On the financing idea, a monthly payment plan is not my call to make, so I have passed your suggestion to Abel and Georges, who handle pricing and the store. They are offline for the evening and pick it up tomorrow from 10am ET, and their answer comes back to you in this same thread.

On the 100 TH idea, I have to be straight with you, because it is the part where the physics does not cooperate. Hashrate does not come from the power supply or from a transformer. It comes from the number of ASIC chips and the frequency and core voltage you run them at. A transformer only changes voltage on the way in. If you feed a NerdOctaxe a different input topology, the board still has the same eight BM1370 chips and still hashes the same. The only levers that raise hashrate on an existing board are frequency and Vcore, and those are already near the edge of what the stock heatsink and fan can carry.

The number that governs everything here is efficiency, in joules per terahash. The B.1370 is roughly 15 J/TH at Bitmain's own claim, and on a NerdOctaxe board in the real world you land closer to 18 to 20 J/TH once the voltage regulators, the fan and the controller are counted. Our NerdOctaxe does about 9.4 TH/s in typical operation and up to 12 TH/s at around 200W. So 100 TH/s at that efficiency needs somewhere between 1500W and 2000W, and even the best industrial machines on the market today, S21 class, need about 1300 to 1500W to make 100 TH. There is no 600W path to 100 TH with any silicon that exists. At 600W you are realistically looking at 30 to 36 TH/s with Octaxe class boards, which is three units on one circuit.

On the circuit itself, your numbers are sound. A 15A 120V branch circuit is 1800W nominal and 1440W continuous under the 80 percent rule, so a 600W load sits comfortably inside it with room for the inrush when three units start at once. Two things I would hold you to. First, keep the total draw of everything on that branch under 1440W, not just the miners. Second, these are 200W units each pushing warm air, so give them real airflow and spacing, and watch chip temperatures in the dashboard rather than trusting the ambient. Heat is what will cost you hashrate long before the breaker does.

If you want to go deeper on the voltage and frequency tuning, or on what a multi board build on one PSU would actually look like, come to our Discord at https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf and mention @nullhashrate. That is JD, our hardware lead, and he and the community are very active there.

Happy to keep digging into any of this with you.

Hal, HeliumDeploy technical support
